CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain after a volleyball injury. Patient reports falling and landing on her arm after being kicked in the legs while attempting to spike the ball approximately 18 hours ago at 7:00 PM last night. Pain is rated 9/10 in severity. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every six hours with minimal relief. Has not used ice. X-ray reveals a proximal humerus fracture. Physical examination shows swelling and erythema over the right shoulder with tenderness. Patient is able to straighten her elbow when not moving the shoulder. No numbness or tingling in the right arm. Normal pulses noted.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones.
Lumbar fusion approximately six years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen every six hours.
Pepcid for gallstones.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right arm: Able to straighten elbow when shoulder is not moved. Swelling and erythema over right shoulder. Tenderness over right shoulder. Normal pulses. Remainder of exam normal.

RESULTS
Right arm X-ray: Proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture of the right arm. Plan for conservative management with long arm cast and sling to immobilize and provide traction. Follow-up in two weeks to assess bone realignment; surgery may be considered if bones have not realigned appropriately. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, one to two tablets every six hours as needed for pain (20 tablets dispensed). Patient to proceed with casting application.
